title: Resolution independence of the derived tensor product
statement:
Fix a scheme $Y$, a commutative ring $A$, and complexes $K_1,K_2$ of $A_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Let $q:P\to K_1$ and $q':P'\to K_1$ be quasi-isomorphisms with K-flat sources [def-weil-derived-tensor]. If a morphism of complexes $\alpha:P\to P'$ is supplied with $q'\alpha$ homotopic to $q$, then
$$\alpha\otimes1_{K_2}:P\otimes_AK_2\longrightarrow P'\otimes_AK_2$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. No such direct comparison morphism is asserted to exist. Without choosing a direct comparison, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$Q(P\otimes_AK_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P'\otimes_AK_2)$$
in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, where $Q$ is the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It depends on the specified resolution maps $q,q'$, agrees with $Q(\alpha\otimes1_{K_2})$ whenever such an $\alpha$ is supplied, is the identity for identical resolutions, and satisfies the cocycle identity for three resolutions. Thus the object $K_1\otimes_A^LK_2$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor] is independent of the chosen K-flat resolution up to this canonical isomorphism.

proof.text: Work in the abelian category of $A_Y$-module sheaves on the small site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. We first prove a more general assertion: any quasi-isomorphism $a:U\to V$ between K-flat complexes remains a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with any complex $F$. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], its cone $C=\operatorname{Cone}(a)$ is acyclic. By the cone clause of [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum], $C$ is also K-flat. Both cited statements apply to this ringed site, without any boundedness or flatness of terms.

By [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary], $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes C)$ is acyclic for arbitrary $F$. By [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] it is the cone, up to a complex isomorphism, of $1_F\otimes a$. The converse cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] makes this map a quasi-isomorphism. To obtain the order $a\otimes1_F$, use the explicit signed swap for the total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]: on the $(p,q)$ summand send $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$. Its square is the identity. Comparing the two differential terms gives respectively the signs $(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^{pq}$ on both sides, so this is a chain isomorphism. Naturality of the module swap conjugates $1_F\otimes a$ to $a\otimes1_F$. Hence both orders preserve quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat sources.

Fix $F=K_2$ and write $\mathsf Q:K(\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y))\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the homotopy-category localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tensoring defines a functor from the homotopy category to the derived category: if $h$ is a homotopy in the first factor, the degree $-1$ map $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes y$ satisfies $dH+Hd=(dh+hd)\otimes1$, because the two terms involving $d_F$ have opposite signs in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a derived morphism between K-flat complexes $U,V$, use the right calculus [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] and [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] to write it as the roof $U\xleftarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{b}V$. Resolve $M$ by $r:R\to M$ using the general ringed-site theorem [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $J(f)=\mathsf Q(f\otimes1_F)$ and assign the roof the morphism $J(br)J(sr)^{-1}$. The composite $sr$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes, so Step 2 supplies its inverse. For two choices, first replace both roofs by their resolved roofs $U\xleftarrow{d_i}R_i\xrightarrow{e_i}V$, where $R_i$ is K-flat, $d_i=s_i r_i$ and $e_i=b_i r_i$. These still represent the original derived arrow since $\mathsf Q(r_i)$ is invertible. Apply [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] to these resolved roofs: there are $a_i:T\to R_i$ with $d_1a_1=d_2a_2$ a quasi-isomorphism and $e_1a_1=e_2a_2$ in the homotopy category. Resolve $T$ by $z:S\to T$ with $S$ K-flat and put $c_i=a_i z$. Each $c_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism: $H^n(d_i)H^n(c_i)=H^n(d_i c_i)$ and both $H^n(d_i)$ and $H^n(d_i c_i)$ are isomorphisms. Step 2 makes $J(c_i)$ invertible. Functoriality and cancellation give $J(e_i)J(d_i)^{-1}=J(e_i c_i)J(d_i c_i)^{-1}$; the right-hand expressions for $i=1,2$ are equal by the common-refinement equations. This proves equality of the assigned arrows, including independence of every intervening K-flat resolution.

proof.text:
The roof assignment of Step 3 respects identities, using the roof with both legs the identity on a K-flat complex. For composition, take K-flat-middle roofs $U\xleftarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{a}V$ and $V\xleftarrow{t}R'\xrightarrow{b}W$. The right-calculus axiom [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] gives $v:T\to R$ a quasi-isomorphism and $w:T\to R'$ with $av=tw$. Resolve $T$ by $z:S\to T$ with $S$ K-flat using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $v_0=vz,w_0=wz$. The composite roof has legs $sv_0,bw_0$. Step 2 inverts $J(s),J(t),J(v_0)$, and $J(a)J(v_0)=J(t)J(w_0)$, since tensor respects composition [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Therefore
$$J(bw_0)J(sv_0)^{-1}=J(b)J(w_0)J(v_0)^{-1}J(s)^{-1}=J(b)J(t)^{-1}J(a)J(s)^{-1}.$$
This is exactly the composite of the two assigned arrows; no invertibility of $w_0$ is needed. Thus Step 3 defines a functor on the full subcategory of the derived category represented by K-flat complexes. Its value on a chain map between such complexes is $J(f)$, by using an identity denominator.

proof.text: In the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the given resolution maps specify the isomorphism $u_{q,q'}=\mathsf Q(q')^{-1}\mathsf Q(q):\mathsf Q(P)\to\mathsf Q(P')$. Apply the functor of Steps 3-4 to obtain $c_{q,q'}:Q(P\otimes F)\to Q(P'\otimes F)$. It is an isomorphism because the functor sends the inverse of $u_{q,q'}$ to an inverse. Cancelling the resolution isomorphisms gives $u_{q,q}=1$ and $u_{q',q''}u_{q,q'}=u_{q,q''}$; functoriality proves the identity and cocycle laws for $c$. If $q'\alpha$ is homotopic to $q$, then $H^n(q')H^n(\alpha)=H^n(q)$ for every $n$, so $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism by cancellation. Step 2 proves the required chain-level assertion. Moreover $\mathsf Q(\alpha)=u_{q,q'}$, and Step 4 identifies its image with $Q(\alpha\otimes1_F)$, proving agreement with the canonical comparison. The two total tensor objects are precisely the prescribed models in [def-weil-derived-tensor], so these comparisons prove independence of the chosen resolution.
